'''Chandima Gomes''' (Sinhala: චන්දිම ගෝමස්) is a Sri Lankan engineer, [[physicist]] and writer who is now working as a distinguished professor of high-voltage engineering at the University of Witwatersrand, Johannesburg, South Africa. He is also a permanent resident of Malaysia. The platform of his research and engineering career is mainly Asia and Africa, where he works on [[lightning protection]], [[Ground (electricity)|grounding]], and [[electromagnetic interference]], on which topics he has put several of his research outputs into practice. Apart from lightning protection and [[electromagnetic compatibility]] that reduces economic losses from natural and man-made threats, he has also been working on human and animal safety against [[lightning]] mainly in developing countries in Asia and Africa.<ref>[http://www.scidev.net/global/disasters/feature/striking-back-lightning-in-the-developing-world.html Striking back: lightning in the developing world, Sci Dev Net, August 2007]</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20131103185419/http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2013/11/131102-lightning-deaths-developing-countries-storms/ National Geographic, November 2 2013]</ref><ref>[http://www.newvision.co.ug/news/639619-entebbe-tororo-more-prone-to-lightning-strikes.html Entebbe, Tororo more prone to lightning strikes, New Vision, February 2014]</ref><ref>[http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=64544 Protection of Archaeological sites in the wrong way, The Island, October 25, 2012]</ref><ref>[https://www.thehindu.com/todays-paper/tp-national/tp-tamilnadu/Improved-methods-suggested-to-map-areas-prone-to-lightning/article14875729.ece Improved methods suggested to map areas prone to lightning, The Hindu, November 15, 2007]</ref> He is also an engineering consultant and trainer in lightning protection, grounding and bonding, electromagnetic interference and research methodology. He has conducted over 120 training programs all over the world.

== Education and early career ==
[[File:Chandima Gomes with his Wife.jpg|frameless|right|Prof. Chandima Gomes with his wife in Sweden in late 90s]]
Gorakanage Arosha Chandima Gomes was born in [[Colombo]], [[Sri Lanka]], on 12 September 1966. He had his education up to secondary level at [[Royal College Colombo|Royal College]]<ref>[http://royalcollege.lk Royal College Sri Lanka]</ref> and then proceeded to [[University of Colombo]],<ref>[http://www.cmb.ac.lk/ University of Colombo Sri Lanka]</ref> where he studied for a special degree in physics. In 1993 he passed out from UoC with first-class honours degree in the field of physics. Soon after his first degree, Gomes joined the UoC as a lecturer in physics and started a joint PhD program with [[Uppsala University]], Sweden.<ref>[http://www.uu.se/ Uppsala University Sweden]</ref> At Uppsala University, he did research in several fields such as lightning physics, high-voltage engineering, discharge physics etc. under the supervision of Vernon Cooray.<ref>[http://www.el.angstrom.uu.se/personer/vernon/Vernon.html Vernon Cooray Home Page Uppsala University]</ref> In 1999, he received his PhD and returned to Sri Lanka. Chandima is also a [[chartered engineer]] and [[Chartered Physicist]] registered in the UK.

From 1999 to 2009, while working as a senior academic and a researcher at UoC, Gomes was involved with several projects in promoting lightning safety and protection in the South Asian region.<ref>[http://www.sari-energy.org/PageFiles/What_We_Do/SmallGrants/Downloads/NewsletterDec05.pdf SARI/Energy (USAID) Report, 2005] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402114932/http://www.sari-energy.org/PageFiles/What_We_Do/SmallGrants/Downloads/NewsletterDec05.pdf |date=April 2, 2015 }}</ref><ref>[http://www.island.lk/2007/05/29/L2.pdf Beyond Frontiers, The Island, 29th May 2007]</ref><ref>[http://www.lightningsafety.com/nlsi_history/intl_safety_initiative.html NLSI International Lightning Safety Initiatives] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150303070012/http://www.lightningsafety.com/nlsi_history/intl_safety_initiative.html |date=March 3, 2015 }}</ref> He was also involved with many commissions in Sri Lanka such as being the chairman of the Young Scientists Forum of NASTEC,<ref>[http://www.nastec.lk/index.php/young-scientists-forum Young Scientists Forum NASTEC Sri Lanka]</ref> chairman of the committee on developing National Policy on Lightning Protection,<ref>[http://www.nastec.lk/ National Science and Technology Commission Sri Lanka]</ref> and Sri Lanka Telecommunication Regulatory Commission's National Policy on Antenna Structures.<ref>[http://www.trc.gov.lk/images/pdf/guide_l.pdf National Policy on Antenna Structures]</ref>

== Career in Malaysia ==

[[File:Chandima Gomes in Uganda.jpg|frameless|right|Gomes after a conference in Uganda]]
Gomes started his career as an engineering consultant in lightning protection and EMI/EMC in the early 2000 and gradually became a trainer on the subject. In 2010 he shifted to Malaysia as a professor of electrical engineering,<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.eng.upm.edu.my/akademikkee#akademikkee |title=Academic Staff Dept Electrical Engineering Universiti Putra Malaysia |access-date=2015-01-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150924000743/http://www.eng.upm.edu.my/akademikkee#akademikkee |archive-date=2015-09-24 |url-status=dead }}</ref> at [[Universiti Putra Malaysia]] (UPM), where he played a key role in establishing the Centre for Electromagnetic and Lightning Protection (CELP)<ref>[http://www.celp.upm.edu.my/index.php/en/ CELP Malaysia] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150108235331/http://www.celp.upm.edu.my/index.php/en/ |date=January 8, 2015 }}</ref> of which Chandima became the first head of the institute.<ref>[http://www.celp.upm.edu.my/index.php/en/features/organization CELP organizational chart] {{webarchive |url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402124845/http://www.celp.upm.edu.my/index.php/en/features/organization |date=April 2, 2015 }}</ref> The CELP, the first of its kind in Asia, is dedicated to research, education, awareness and training on lightning-related engineering and physics.

After his work in promoting lightning safety in Asia, he started working in the same line in Africa where the annual lightning death is extremely high.<ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20131103185419/http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2013/11/131102-lightning-deaths-developing-countries-storms/ National Geographic, November 2 In November 2018, Gomes shifted to South Africa, becoming the chair of the ESKOM Power Plant Engineering Institute (EPPEI)-HVAC and a professor of high-voltage engineering at the University of Witwatersrand.

== Achievements ==

In 2014, with over 10 years of research, Gomes made an explanation on the lightning protection technology of ancient Sri Lankan Buddhist monuments, called [[stupa]]; very large hemispherical/conical buildings constructed 1500–2000 years ago. Although the [[Mahavamsa|Mahawamsa]], the "Great Chronicle" of Sri Lankan history, written in the first few centuries A.D., has also mentioned that these stupa have been provided with lightning protection by Sri Lankan kings, until Chandima's work there was no scientifically sound explanation given on the methodology.<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.rivira.lk/epaper/sunday/2015/01/25/index.html#17/z |title=Ranweli Sayen Mathuwana Akunu Thakshanaya (in Sinhala Language) |access-date=2015-02-16 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150127104330/http://www.rivira.lk/epaper/sunday/2015/01/25/index.html#17/z |archive-date=2015-01-27 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref>[https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/xpl/articleDetails.jsp?tp=&arnumber=6973392&searchWithin%3Dgomes%26queryText%3DICLP+2014 Lightning current and voltage distribution of large axially symmetric Buddhist stupa in Sri Lanka]</ref><ref>[https://ieeexplore.ieee.org/xpl/articleDetails.jsp?tp=&arnumber=6973441&searchWithin%3Dgomes%26queryText%3DICLP+2014 Lightning; Gods and Sciences]</ref>

Ideas depicted in many general articles contributed by Gomes have already been put into practice in several countries.<ref>[http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=42126 Milking the Southern Expressway, The Island, December 29, 2011]</ref><ref>[https://web.archive.org/web/20131103185419/http://news.nationalgeographic.com/news/2013/11/131102-lightning-deaths-developing-countries-storms/ National Geographic, November 2 2013]</ref><ref>[http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=70693 Mother-Care Centers, The Island, January 20, 2013]</ref><ref>[http://www.island.lk/index.php?code_title=100468&page=article-details&page_cat=article-details The Next Alien Attack, The Island, March 25 2014]</ref><ref>[http://www.island.lk/index.php?page_cat=article-details&page=article-details&code_title=69636 City of Universities, The Island, January 04 2013]</ref>

Chandima Gomes has also authored the Sinhala book "The pathway to be rich" (Sinhala: ධනවතෙකු වීමේ මග), which is now in wide circulation among Sinhala readers in both Sri Lanka and abroad.<ref>[https://www.researchgate.net/profile/Chandima_Gomes/publication/274956735_Dhanawatheku_Weeme_Maga_The_pathway_to_be_rich/links/552d339c0cf21acb09214536/Dhanawatheku-Weeme-Maga-The-pathway-to-be-rich.pdf   ධනවතෙකු වීමේ මග]. {{ISBN|978-955-42008-0-7}}</ref>
